title: Methanol-water, 40 vol%
brief: methanol-water, 40 vol% methanol at 293.15 K, 101325 Pa (volume fractions of the pure liquids measured separately at the stated temperature, before mixing)
disclaimers: Responses are the recorded PubChem / NIST WebBook fetches (hash-checked), replayed offline.
The mixture density is not the ideal-mixing value: the excess volume is unknown from these sources and needs a measurement.
caveats: State: 293.15 K and 101325 Pa only; every pure-component value is NIST's at exactly this state.
Composition basis: volume fractions of the pure liquids measured separately at the stated temperature, before mixing.
methanol: phase at the state "liquid"; NIST normal boiling point 337.632 K.
water: phase at the state "liquid"; NIST normal boiling point 373.1243 K.
The ideal-mixing values are a model with no excess volume or heat capacity; they are reported under their own subject and are not the mixture's properties.
PubChem values are contributed records: kept with their contributor and location, cross-checked, never averaged; disagreements are queued for review.

physicalTests: liquid density: density of the liquid by digital density meter at the stated temperature [[object Object]] — the excess volume on mixing is not known from these sources, so the mixture's density is not the ideal-mixing value

specific heat capacity: specific heat capacity by DSC over the stated temperature range (sealed pans for a volatile liquid) [[object Object]] — the excess heat capacity is not known from these sources
dynamic viscosity: kinematic viscosity at the stated temperature, times the measured density for dynamic viscosity [[object Object]] — no mixing rule for viscosity is validated here for this mixture

liquid thermal conductivity: transient hot wire; the standard's scope is engine coolants and related fluids, so the laboratory confirms it applies [[object Object]] — no mixing rule for thermal conductivity is validated here for this mixture
flash point: closed-cup flash point (Tag) of the exact liquid [[object Object]] — a mixture's flash point is not the mole- or mass-weighted pure values; only a test establishes it

normal boiling point: distillation range at the stated pressure (initial boiling point and range; not an equilibrium bubble point) [[object Object]] — vapour-liquid equilibrium is not modelled: the mixture's bubble point is not computed
